Janet —

Quick read and a few recommendations below. I also uploaded a small CSV (karthik-latam-indexing-sheet.csv) that shows the mapping I usually use when converting contractor rates to local FTE bands for São Paulo and Buenos Aires. Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A2bLatamIndexingExample

High level:
- Prefer local-banding (not US equivalent) for contractors who have been paid locally and will remain in-country.
- Convert contractor daily/weekly rate to an annualized local gross figure, then index to our Level 3–6 band floors using a 0.85–1.10 multiplier depending on seniority and retention risk.
- For senior ICs (Level 5+), use regional premium + 10% to match scarce skills in São Paulo.

Suggested offer range (rough guidance, final depends on benefits & taxes):
- Level 3 (junior/mid): BRL 140k–190k
- Level 4 (mid): BRL 190k–260k
- Level 5 (senior): BRL 260k–360k (+10% premium possible)

Approvals: any band above the Level 4 midpoint requires manager + People BP (Laura) sign-off; exceptions >10% above band cap require People + Finance approval.

Laura / Marissa — I want to flag this for policy confirmation: this candidate will be the program manager for a paid pilot with Greenfield; they asked for local-market anchor rather than US-remote comp. Can we confirm the exception workflow and whether we want to compress Level 4–5 overlap for LATAM hires given market movement?

Cheers,
Karthik

Thanks, that mapping looks sensible. A couple of policy items and an ask:

Policy notes:
- We should treat LATAM conversions as local-hire by default when the contractor is on local payroll and will remain in-country.
- For Q2–Q3 2027 we are seeing upward pressure in São Paulo for cloud infra/product roles; recommend a temporary 5–12% upward band adjustment (time-boxed through end of Q3) for critical hires to avoid losing offers to local comp.
- We will not change band definitions globally; this is a regional indexing overlay. We need documented rationale and retention metrics for any extension.

Ask: please attach the latest market report (I pulled a brief) — I put it in the thread: latam-benchmarks-q2-2027.pdf. Marissa, can you confirm whether we want to pilot compressing overlap between Level 4 cap and Level 5 floor for LATAM hires to reduce negotiation friction? If yes, propose an experiment window and metrics (time-to-accept, offer acceptance rate).
